item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find a single 2024 speech or document that functions as a full formal doctrine. The evidence is distributed across speeches, cabinet instructions, IMF/World Bank-backed reform language, and repression reports. So the gap is not absence of a governing program, but absence of a clean, unified ideological manifesto.","evidence":[{"title":"Sisi takes the constitutional oath for a new presidential term","publisher":"Presidency of the Republic of Egypt","date":"Apr. 2, 2024","url":"https://www.presidency.eg/en/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/event242024/","summary":"Sisi framed the new term as a continuation of building a “modern and democratic state,” which is explicit self-description of governing purpose and direction. It is self-justifying, but still useful as revealed program language.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"President El-Sisi meets prime minister and members of the new government","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"Jul. 3, 2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-meets-prime-minister-and-members-of-the-new-government/","summary":"Sisi told the cabinet to strengthen institutional frameworks, improve inter-agency coordination, and emphasize integrity and transparency. That is explicit governing direction and a bureaucratic reform program, not just general rhetoric.","question_ids":["8B.1"]},{"title":"President Sisi swears in new government ministers","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"Jul. 3, 2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-sisi-swears-in-new-government-ministers/","summary":"The reshuffle installed a broad cabinet with technocratic portfolios tied to economic management, energy, science, and foreign affairs. This suggests a program of managed technocracy and policy specialization.","question_ids":["8B.1"]},{"title":"IMF staff and authorities reach agreement on reviews under the EFF","publisher":"IMF","date":"Mar. 6, 2024","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/06/pr-2459-egypt-staff-and-authorities-reach-agreement-on-reviews-under-the-eff-arrangement","summary":"The government agreed to flexible exchange rates, tighter macro policy, more social spending for vulnerable groups, and reforms to level the playing field. That reveals a concrete economic program: stabilization, redistribution at the margin, and reduced favoritism toward state firms.","question_ids":["8B.1"]},{"title":"IMF reaches agreement on the 3rd review of the EFF","publisher":"IMF","date":"Jun. 6, 2024","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/06/pr-24208-egypt-imf-reaches-agreement-on-the-3rd-review-of-the-eff","summary":"The reform agenda was explicitly framed around private-sector-led growth, fiscal space for health and education, and reducing the state’s role. This is one of the clearest public statements of the government’s 2024 strategic economic direction.","question_ids":["8B.1"]},{"title":"Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt through Cash Transfer Programs","publisher":"World Bank","date":"May 28, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs","summary":"Takaful and Karama is described as institutionalized, well-targeted, and linked to health, education, and women’s empowerment, with a 55 percent benefit increase. This supports a coherent social-protection program rather than pure patronage.","question_ids":["8B.1"]},{"title":"Women’s Empowerment Strategy 2030","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"Mar. 12, 2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/strategies/womens-empowerment-strategy-2030/","summary":"The presidency assigned the strategy to government and state agencies, framing equal opportunity, labor participation, legal protection, and social integration as state priorities. This is explicit program language with a stated policy direction.","question_ids":["8B.1"]},{"title":"President El-Sisi’s speech at the official ceremony of laying the foundation stone for power unit 4 at El-Dabaa nuclear power plant","publisher":"State Information Service","date":"Jan. 23, 2024","url":"https://sis.gov.eg/en/presidency/speeches-telegrams-posts/el-sisi-s-speech-at-the-official-ceremony-of-laying-the-foundation-stone-for-power-unit-4-at-el-dabaa-nuclear-power-plant/","summary":"Sisi described peaceful nuclear power as a strategic, long-term energy-security project tied to development and reduced fossil dependence. This is a clear stated policy program, albeit in a narrow sector.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.3"]},{"title":"President El-Sisi and Abdullah II call for an immediate Gaza ceasefire","publisher":"Presidency of the Republic of Egypt","date":"Apr. 1, 2024","url":"https://www.presidency.eg/en/%D9%82%D8%B3%D9%85_%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1/%D8%A3%D8%AE%D8%A8%D8%A7%D8%B1-%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D9%8A%D8%A9/new142024-2/","summary":"Sisi publicly framed Egypt’s role around immediate ceasefire, civilian protection, and preventing wider war. This reveals a strategic external line: de-escalation and mediation rather than maximalist confrontation.","question_ids":["8B.1"]},{"title":"Egypt’s reform agenda is aimed at inclusive growth and protection of the poorest","publisher":"World Bank Group","date":"Mar. 18, 2024","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2024/03/18/world-bank-group-statement-of-support-to-egypt-s-development-and-reform-efforts","summary":"The World Bank described the agenda as private-sector job creation, human capital, resilience, and protection of the poorest and most vulnerable. This is indirect but useful corroboration of a coherent governing program.","question_ids":["8B.1"]},{"title":"Egypt: Civic Space Under Siege","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"Jan. 11, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/egypt-civic-space-under-siege","summary":"HRW said Egypt curtailed free expression and peaceful assembly ahead of the vote to stymie meaningful competition. That reveals a governing goal of preserving control over the political field, which can be evaluated against later repression.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"Egypt: Court Punishes Activists Challenging al-Sisi","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"Feb. 8, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/02/08/egypt-court-punishes-activists-challenging-al-sisi","summary":"The court sentence and election ban for Tantawy and supporters show the regime’s practical program included deterring opposition challenge, not just running a neutral election system.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"Egypt: Spate of Free Speech Prosecutions","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"Aug. 29, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/29/egypt-spate-free-speech-prosecutions","summary":"HRW reported renewed prosecutions of critics and journalists, including reporting tied to a corruption investigation involving senior pro-Sisi party members. This suggests a revealed goal of shielding the ruling network from scrutiny.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"Egypt: Halt crackdown on people voicing concerns over economic crisis","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"May 13, 2024","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/egypt-halt-crackdown-on-people-voicing-concerns-over-economic-crisis/","summary":"Authorities arrested protesters and online critics over economic discontent. That shows the regime’s practical strategy still relied on coercion when criticism became politically costly.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"Egypt: More than 100 arbitrarily detained over calls for anti-government protests","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"Jul. 18, 2024","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/07/egypt-more-than-100-arbitrarily-detained-over-calls-for-anti-government-protests/","summary":"Security forces detained 119 people after protest calls over prices and power cuts. This is strong revealed-goal evidence of regime maintenance through repression, not open contestability.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]},{"title":"Freedom in the World 2024: Egypt","publisher":"Freedom House","date":"2024","url":"https://freedomhouse.org/country/egypt/freedom-world/2024","summary":"Freedom House says Sisi and the security apparatus dominate policymaking, the corruption watchdog is controlled by Sisi, and meaningful opposition is virtually nonexistent. This reveals an information-control component in the governing program.","question_ids":["8B.1","8B.2"]}]}
